title: First response to the undervolt
question: Main bus B is undervolt and the fuel cells are sagging. What do you tell the crew first?

options.text: Cut electrical load: power down about 10 amps using the emergency pink pages of the checklist.
Try to restart all three fuel cells right away.
Fire the main engine now and head straight home.

evidence.query: power down delta of 10 amps pink pages emergency checklist

title: Chasing the leak
question: Telemetry shows oxygen flowing out through fuel cell 3. What do you ask the crew to do?

options.text: Open the cross-feed so oxygen tank 1 can supply fuel cell 3.
Close the reactant (REAC) valve on fuel cell 3 to try to stop the leak.
Ignore it; fuel cells 1 and 2 can carry the load.

evidence.query: losing O2 flow fuel cell 3 close the REAC valve

title: The lifeboat
question: Oxygen tank 1 is now slowly going to zero too. Odyssey will soon have no power or oxygen. What do you start planning?

options.text: Stay in Odyssey and ration oxygen and power.
Separate from the lunar module to save weight.
Move the crew into the lunar module Aquarius and use it as a lifeboat.

evidence.query: O2 tank 1 going to zero LM lifeboat

title: Getting back on a path home
question: Apollo 13 left the free-return path to aim for the landing site. The service module engine sits next to the explosion. How do you put them back on a path home?

options.text: Fire the service module's big engine (SPS) for a fast direct abort.
Use the lunar module's descent engine (DPS) for a midcourse burn back to free return.
Do nothing and let the Moon's gravity bring them home.

evidence.query: P30 maneuver pad midcourse correction for free return Aquarius burn

title: Speeding up after the Moon
question: On free return the trip home is long. A burn two hours after passing behind the Moon (PC+2) could shorten it. What do you plan?

options.text: Plan a PC+2 burn with the descent engine to speed up the return.
No burn: save every drop of fuel and accept the longer trip.
Turn around before reaching the Moon.

evidence.query: PC plus 2 maneuver pad DPS burn

title: The CO2 crisis
question: The lunar module's CO2 filters can't last for three people, and the command module's square canisters don't fit the LM's round sockets. What do you do?

options.text: Move the crew back into the command module.
Rely on the two spare cartridges in the spacesuit backpacks.
Have the crew build an adapter from command module canisters, hoses, cardboard and tape: the "mailbox".

evidence.query: command module LiOH canisters connect hoses mailbox procedure

title: The separation order
question: Before re-entry the crew must leave the damaged service module and the lunar module behind. What is the plan?

options.text: Charge Odyssey's battery from the LM, jettison the service module first, then the LM, then re-enter in Odyssey.
Jettison the LM first and re-enter with the service module still attached.
Re-enter inside the lunar module.

evidence.query: charge the battery in CSM jettison the service module LM jettison entry
